claims.limitation: This verifies the implemented projection invariant on one synthetic matrix, not trained-model stability relative to HC.
claims.observation: A seeded 4x4 CPU projection was nonnegative and doubly stochastic; its measured spectral norm was 1.
claims.text: mHC constrains hyper-connection residual mappings by projecting them onto a manifold to preserve stability relative to unconstrained HC (Figure 1, Section 4.1).

claims.limitation: This tests dimensional consistency only; it does not reproduce Table 1 task quality or trained component ablations.
claims.observation: 216 of 216 seeded synthetic-tensor rows preserved their expected output shape across eight mapping variants.
claims.text: HC component ablations test the roles of pre, post, and residual mappings while maintaining dimensional consistency with fixed mappings (Table 1).

claims.limitation: This tests only a toy residual-propagation mechanism; it does not reproduce loss gaps, trained gradient norms, or the paper's model-scale figures.
claims.observation: Computed 27 paired seeded raw/projected residual-matrix compositions at depths 10, 50, and 100.
claims.text: Training and propagation analyses show unconstrained HC has larger loss gaps, gradient norms, and residual propagation instability than mHC (Figure 2, Figure 3, Figure 5, Figure 7).
